items.stem: You need to combine a customer table and an orders table on a shared CustomerID, keeping only matching rows. Which tool fits?

options.rationale: Correct: the Join tool matches rows on a key and outputs matched records from its J anchor.
The Formula tool creates or edits columns; it does not join tables.
Summarize aggregates; it does not join on a key.
Sample returns a subset of rows; it does not combine tables.

items.stem: Which tool reshapes data from a wide layout into a tall key-value layout?

options.rationale: Correct: Transpose pivots columns into rows (wide to tall).
Cross Tab does the reverse, turning rows into columns.
Select renames or reorders fields; it does not reshape.

items.stem: Which TWO help an Alteryx workflow run reliably when scheduled on Server? (Select TWO)

options.text: Use relative or configurable paths rather than hard-coded local paths
options.rationale: Correct: configurable paths keep the workflow working after deployment.

options.text: Parameterize inputs with interface tools where needed
options.rationale: Correct: interface tools let inputs be supplied at run time.
Removing output tools means the workflow produces nothing.

options.text: Rely on files that exist only on the developer's laptop
options.rationale: Local-only files are unavailable to the Server and will fail.

items.explanation: Correct: configurable paths keep the workflow working after deployment.; Correct: interface tools let inputs be supplied at run time.
